# OTPInput

Figma: [03b. OTPInput](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-897) · Family: 03 Form & Input · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-20

A multi-box input for OTP, verification, and PIN code entry. Each digit lives in its own bordered square. The currently active box gets a focus ring and dark border so users always know where the next digit goes. Used on Nafath verification, login OTP, transaction confirmation, and 2FA flows.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/otp-input/reference.png`

### OTP Input

A row of 4 or 6 square digit boxes for one-time codes, with a clear focus ring on the active box. Used for SMS login OTP, Nafath, 2FA and confirming high-value investments or withdrawals.

Level: organism

Use when:
- SMS OTP after login or phone change: Length=4
- Authenticator or 6-digit codes: Length=6 (Size=md on narrow phones)
- Confirming a withdrawal to IBAN or a large investment

Don't use when:
- Phone number entry: use Input Phone
- Passwords or longer codes: use Input
- Small quantities: use NumericStepper

Accessibility: Keep digits visible on error instead of clearing them, and set State=disabled during verification to stop duplicate submissions.

> Not published to the Figma library. Use it by name everywhere; in another Figma file take its published route or copy it from the Syntropy file (syntropy-components, unpublished.md).

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

OTP Input is the standard component for capturing short numeric codes - typically 4 or 6 digits - used to verify identity or confirm a transaction. Each digit gets its own visible box with a clear focus indicator so users can see exactly where they are in the entry sequence.

On Safqah, OTP Input shows up on: Nafath verification (Saudi national ID), login OTP sent via SMS, transaction confirmation codes for high-value investments, 2FA setup, and password recovery. The 4-digit variant is more common for SMS OTP (matches what banks send); 6-digit for authenticator-app TOTP codes.

### At a glance

| Partial · typing in progress | Complete · all digits entered | Error · code rejected |
| --- | --- | --- |

### Anatomy

Each OTP Input is a horizontal row of square digit boxes with consistent gaps. Visually simple, but the active-box treatment is what makes it usable - without a clear focus indicator users lose track of where they are.

| Digit box (square) Bordered square container. 56dp at lg, 48dp at md. Radius/8 corners match Input Field. Inside-aligned 1dp border at rest, 2dp dark border when focused. | Digit text IBM Plex Sans Medium, font 20 at lg / 18 at md. Centered horizontally and vertically. text/default color in all active states. | Gap between boxes Spacing/12 at lg, Spacing/8 at md. Boxes never touch - the visual separation reinforces "each box is one digit, in order". | Focus indicator On the currently active box: border switches to border/focus and weight becomes 2dp. Combined with strokeAlign INSIDE so the focus stays within the box bounds. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

### Lengths - 4 or 6 digits

Two lengths cover the two common OTP scenarios: 4-digit for SMS-based OTP from telcos and Saudi banks (most common), 6-digit for TOTP authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy) and international standards. Pick the length that matches what your backend actually generates and verifies.

4 digits

SMS OTP (most banks, Nafath, Absher), bank transaction confirmation codes, signup verification. The default for Saudi consumer flows.

6 digits

TOTP authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy, Microsoft Authenticator), 2FA backup codes, higher-security flows. International standard.

### States

Five states cover the full lifecycle of OTP entry. The partial state is the most visually complex - it shows both completed boxes (with digits) and the currently active box (with focus ring) plus remaining empty boxes.

empty

Initial state when the screen loads. All boxes empty with subtle gray borders. The first box should auto-focus (handled at app level).

partial

Mid-entry. Completed boxes show their digit with a stronger border. The next empty box gets the focus ring + 2dp dark border showing where the next digit goes.

complete

All digits entered. All boxes show their values with stronger borders. The app should validate and either accept (proceed) or reject (switch to error state).

error

Code rejected. All boxes get a red border, digits stay visible so the user can see what they entered. Combine with helper text or toast explaining the error.

disabled

Inert state. Gray fill, no digits, no focus. Use when the OTP has timed out and user must request a new one, or while the app is verifying.

### Sizes

Two sizes match the surrounding form density. lg (56dp boxes) for primary OTP screens - Nafath verification, login OTP, the main moment-of-truth flows. md (48dp) for compact dialogs and re-auth modals where vertical space is tight.

Large (56dp boxes, gap 12)

Primary OTP screens. Most visible, easiest to tap. Default for full-screen verification flows on mobile.

Medium (48dp boxes, gap 8)

Compact dialogs, re-auth modals, inline OTP within a longer form. Still meets WCAG touch target.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

OTP Input handles Arabic RTL contexts. In LTR, digits fill left-to-right (typing 1234 shows boxes as 1,2,3,4). In RTL, digits fill right-to-left visually (the first digit lands in the rightmost box). The cursor/active box position adapts to the direction.

LTR

Default. First digit lands in the leftmost box. Active cursor moves left → right with each digit. Standard for English contexts.

RTL

Arabic context. First digit lands in the rightmost box (visually). Active cursor moves right → left. Natural for Arabic numerals reading flow on Nafath, Saudi banks, etc.

### Code examples

How to consume OTP Input in production code.

### Flutter - 4-digit SMS OTP with auto-paste

```dart
// Standard 4-digit OTP for SMS verification
SafqahOTPInput(
  length: 4,
  size: SafqahOTPSize.lg,
  autofillHints: const [AutofillHints.oneTimeCode],
  onCompleted: (code) async {
    final result = await _verifyOTP(code);
    if (!result.success) {
      setState(() => _otpState = SafqahOTPState.error);
      _showErrorToast(result.message);
    }
  },
)
```

### Flutter - 6-digit TOTP for 2FA

```dart
// 6-digit TOTP from authenticator app
SafqahOTPInput(
  length: 6,
  size: SafqahOTPSize.lg,
  autofillHints: const [AutofillHints.oneTimeCode],
  onCompleted: (code) => _verifyTOTP(code),
)
```

### Flutter - RTL Arabic context

```dart
// Nafath verification - Arabic RTL
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: SafqahOTPInput(
    length: 4,
    size: SafqahOTPSize.lg,
    autofillHints: const [AutofillHints.oneTimeCode],
    onCompleted: _verifyNafath,
  ),
)
```

### Flutter - Error state with retry

```dart
// Wrong code rejected by backend
SafqahOTPInput(
  length: 4,
  size: SafqahOTPSize.lg,
  state: SafqahOTPState.error,
  initialValue: lastEnteredCode, // keep what user typed visible
  helperText: 'Wrong code - try again or request a new one',
  onChanged: (code) {
    setState(() => _otpState = SafqahOTPState.partial);
  },
)
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts.

- **Do** · Mid-entry feedback: Show clear visual progress: filled boxes have stronger borders, the active box has a 2dp dark focus ring. Users always know where they are.
- **Don't** · Mid-entry feedback: Don't leave all boxes identical during entry. Without a focus ring users lose track and start tapping random boxes, or worse, double-tapping.
- **Do** · Wrong code rejected: Error state with red borders + digits still visible. User can see what they entered and decide whether to fix one digit or start over.
- **Don't** · Wrong code rejected: Don't auto-clear all boxes on failure. Users lose context, can't see if they typed the wrong digit or were sent the wrong code. Frustrating cycle.
- **Do** · Arabic - Nafath verification: RTL direction. First digit enters the rightmost box, focus moves leftward. Matches Arabic reading flow on Nafath and Saudi bank flows.
- **Don't** · Arabic - Nafath verification: Don't use LTR direction in Arabic contexts. The first typed digit goes to the leftmost box - opposite of what Arabic users expect, breaks muscle memory.
- **Do** · Verification in progress: Disabled state during async verification or when OTP has expired. Gray fill clearly signals the field is inert. Pair with a spinner or countdown.
- **Don't** · Verification in progress: Don't leave the field in active state during async verification - users may keep tapping/typing thinking the request didn't register, triggering duplicate verification calls.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Info:** OTP Input is a single organism - no atomic decomposition like Input. Each digit box is too simple to warrant being its own atom, and OTP is conceptually one component (a code, not a set of independent characters). Build it as one piece and let the variant axes handle the combinations.

> **Info:** The OTP code TEXT property exists at the variant level (default value differs per State for visual demos). At runtime, the Flutter widget actually manages digit state internally - the prop here is just for design-time mocking, not the actual data model.

> **Info:** Focus ring is 2dp INSIDE stroke on the active box. INSIDE alignment keeps the ring within the box bounds - important since boxes sit close together. If we used OUTSIDE alignment the focus rings would overlap adjacent boxes when active.

> **Warning:** FONT WARNING - Same as the rest of the input family: digit text uses IBM Plex Sans Medium since Font/Family/Base resolves to IBM Plex Sans Arabic which isn't installed. Re-bind when Arabic font is installed.

> **Info:** Digit font sizes (20dp lg / 18dp md) are raw px values, not bound to a font/size token. The semantic typography collection doesn't have a font/size/20 token. If you add one later, re-bind these digit text nodes.

> **Tip:** sm size NOT included. OTP boxes need a minimum tap target - going below 48dp makes mis-taps too frequent for a moment-of-truth flow. If you need a super-compact OTP layout (e.g. inline within a settings row), reconsider whether OTP entry even belongs there.

> **Warning:** For 6-digit OTP in tight layouts, the total horizontal space at lg is 6×56 + 5×12 = 396dp, at md it's 6×48 + 5×8 = 328dp. On a 360dp-wide phone (smaller Androids), the lg 6-digit variant overflows. Drop to md or build a custom 5+1 layout for very narrow screens.
